name: iecode
description: Structured Text for TwinCAT in VS Code: edit .TcPOU/.TcDUT/.TcGVL/.TcIO as plain ST, browse and extend PLC projects, workspaces with libraries and applications, view and edit .TcVIS visualizations, text lists (.TcGTLO), image pools (.TcIPO) and the visualization manager (.TcVMO), build and deploy with the iecode CLI.
author: Jan Junklewitz

untrustedWorkspaces.description: IECode runs the iecode CLI and git on the workspace's projects.

customEditors.displayName: IECode Text List / Image Pool / Task / Visualization Manager Editor

commands.title: Save All PLC Projects as Libraries…

iecode.configDiff.hidden.markdownDescription: Categories and noise kinds hidden in **Config Changes** (the checkboxes in the panel write this setting).

iecode.openAsST.description: Open TwinCAT object files as Structured Text instead of XML.

iecode.greenComments.description: Show comments in Structured Text green, also in themes that render comments grey. Not applied in high contrast themes; turn off to use the theme's (or your own token) colors.

iecode.cliPath.markdownDescription: Path to the `iecode` CLI. Empty: `iecode` from PATH.

iecode.tcVersion.markdownDescription: TwinCAT version for build and activate: `auto`, `4024`, `4026` or an exact build like `4024.66`.

iecode.platforms.markdownDescription: Target platforms to build, e.g. `TwinCAT RT (x64)`. Empty: the active platform.

iecode.restartAfterActivate.description: Restart TwinCAT in run mode after activating.

iecode.libraryOutput.description: Folder (relative to the solution) for saved libraries.

iecode.showXae.description: Show the TwinCAT XAE window while the CLI works (debugging).

iecode.libraryRepository.markdownDescription: TwinCAT library repository folder (`<vendor>/<library>/<version>`). Empty: `%TWINCAT3DIR%\Components\Plc\Managed Libraries`.

iecode.librarySources.markdownDescription: Extra folders with library files named `<Name>_<Version>.library` (e.g. a shared drive).

enumDescriptions: Claude Code when installed, else GitHub Copilot Chat, else the clipboard.
Open GitHub Copilot Chat with the context prefilled (you send it).
Copy the context and open Claude Code; paste it there.
Only copy the context to the clipboard.
iecode.aiChat.markdownDescription: Where **Add to AI Chat** and **Comment for AI…** send code and visualization elements.

enumDescriptions: Open the IECode output when a CLI command (build, check, activate …) starts.
Open it only when a command fails or reports warnings.
Don't open it by itself (View › Output › IECode).
iecode.revealOutput.markdownDescription: When the **IECode** output channel opens by itself. It lists every CLI run with its progress, the compiler errors, warnings and messages, and the result; filter by level in the Output view.

iecode.ads.target.markdownDescription: Target of the **ADS Watch** view: `local` or an AMS NetId (six numbers, e.g. `192.168.1.10.1.1`). Changing it reconnects.

iecode.ads.port.markdownDescription: ADS port of the PLC runtime for the **ADS Watch** view (`851` = first PLC of TwinCAT 3). Changing it reconnects.

iecode.ads.sampleIntervalMs.markdownDescription: How often watched ADS values are read, in milliseconds. Windows timers tick about every 15.6 ms, so below ~16 ms the real rate is lower; every sample carries its actual read time.

iecode.ads.bufferSeconds.markdownDescription: Seconds of watched ADS values kept for the scope and AI tools. Long windows with many variables keep fewer seconds (at most 2 million values).

enumDescriptions: AI tools cannot write PLC variables.

You confirm each AI write. Claude Code writes always show IECode's own dialog. In Copilot Chat this relies on you not choosing "Always Allow" for the ADS Write tool: VS Code then skips the confirmation, and extensions cannot prevent that.

Auto-approve: IECode writes without asking (each write is logged in the IECode output). VS Code may still ask by its own tool approval rules. While the workspace or workspace folder settings set iecode.ads.target or iecode.ads.port to something else than your user settings, each write is confirmed instead, so a cloned repository cannot choose where auto-approved writes go. The ADS Watch view shows "AI writes: auto".
iecode.ads.aiWrites.markdownDescription: Whether AI tools (GitHub Copilot Chat in agent mode, Claude Code) may write PLC variables over ADS. User settings only, so a workspace cannot turn it on. Set it with **IECode: Set AI Write Access…** in the ADS Watch view.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No TwinCAT projects found in this workspace.
Open a folder with a .sln, .tsproj or .plcproj, or add one to the workspace.
[Open Folder](command:vscode.openFolder)

No variables watched. Add PLC variables to see their live values over ADS (target: iecode.ads.target).
[Add Variable…](command:iecode.adsWatchAdd)
Or right-click a variable in the ST editor › Add to ADS Watch.

languageModelTools.name: iecode_ads_symbols
languageModelTools.userDescription: Find PLC variables (ADS names and types) in the build output of the workspace PLC projects.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists ADS symbol names and their types from the build output (.tmc) of the TwinCAT PLC projects in the workspace whose name contains the filter (case-insensitive), at most 100. Use it to find the exact ADS name (e.g. MAIN.fbMotor.bEnable) before watching, reading or writing a variable. Projects that were never built are reported as not listed.

filter.description: Part of the ADS name to search for, e.g. "MAIN." or "nCounter"; empty lists the first 100.

languageModelTools.name: iecode_ads_watch
languageModelTools.userDescription: Add or remove PLC variables in the ADS Watch list (live values).
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Adds or removes ADS symbols in the ADS Watch list, whose values are then sampled continuously (every iecode.ads.sampleIntervalMs, default 100 ms) for the read and scope tools. Returns what the call added and removed plus the count; call it with no arguments, or with list: true, for the full list with types and per-symbol errors. Entries you add are marked as added by AI; you can remove only those, unless you pass force: true with remove, which asks the user once to confirm removing their entries. clearAi: true removes all entries you added. Entries can be put in named groups (add with group); a group can be switched off (group with enable: false) so its symbols are not sampled but stay in the list, or removed (group with removeGroup: true). A symbol in two groups is sampled while one of them is on. Watch a variable before asking for its history.

add.description: ADS names to watch, e.g. MAIN.nCounter.

remove.description: ADS names to stop watching (only entries added by AI).

list.description: Return the full list with types and errors. Default: only what this call changed, plus the count.

clearAi.description: Remove every entry you added (the user's entries stay; entries a running wait uses stay until it ends). Cannot be combined with add or remove.

force.description: With remove: also remove entries the user added, after the user confirmed in a dialog. Without it only your own entries can be removed.

group.description: Name of a group. With add: the added symbols join the group (and a switched-off group is switched on). With enable or removeGroup: the group to switch or remove. Only entries you added can be in a group.

enable.description: With group: true samples the group again, false stops sampling its symbols without removing them.

removeGroup.description: With group: remove the group and the entries that belong to no other group.

languageModelTools.name: iecode_ads_read
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read current values of PLC variables over ADS.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the current values of ADS symbols on the configured target (iecode.ads.target). Watched symbols come from the live sample buffer, others are read once. Without symbols, all watched symbols are returned.

symbols.description: ADS names to read; default all watched symbols.

languageModelTools.name: iecode_ads_scope
languageModelTools.userDescription: Summarize how watched PLC variables changed over the last seconds.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns per watched ADS symbol over the last seconds (default 60): min, max, last value and sample count, how often it changed and when, plus a tab-separated table (time in seconds relative to the newest sample). Prefer changesOnly: true for step counters, enums, BOOLs and STRING values (one row per value change with the start value, never thinned; the plain table lists STRING values only in the summary). Use edges: true for BOOL pulses (rising and falling edges with times). maxRows limits the rows, decimals rounds fractions. A plain table over a long window is thinned and says how many samples it shows; it keeps every value change except in fast-changing columns, which are thinned evenly. Only watched symbols have a history: add them with the watch tool first and wait for samples.

symbols.description: Watched ADS names; default all watched symbols.

decimals.description: Round fractional numbers to this many decimals, 0-9 (integers stay as they are).

changesOnly.description: One row per value change instead of one per sample; also lists STRING values. Never thinned.

edges.description: List rising and falling edges of BOOL symbols with their times instead of the table; other types are named as ignored. Do not combine with changesOnly.

languageModelTools.name: iecode_ads_wait
languageModelTools.userDescription: Wait until a watched PLC variable meets a condition.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Waits until an ADS symbol meets a condition, then returns the time and value; returns at once if the condition is already true at the first sample after the call. Conditions: = v, <> v, < v, <= v, > v, >= v, changes, contains "text". v is a number, TRUE/FALSE, an enum name, or a quoted string for STRING values. The symbol is added to the watch list for the duration of the wait if it is not watched. Resolution is the sample interval: a change shorter than one sample can be missed. Not met within the timeout is a normal result with the last value.

condition.description: Condition, e.g. = TRUE, > 5.5, changes or contains "text".

languageModelTools.name: iecode_ads_write
languageModelTools.userDescription: Write a value to a PLC variable over ADS (per iecode.ads.aiWrites; off by default). With "confirm" each write is confirmed unless you choose "Always Allow" for this tool.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Writes a value to an ADS symbol on the configured target and returns the value read back. This changes a running machine or PLC: only write when the user asked for it. Values are plain text in this format, not IEC 61131-3 literals (no T#1S, no 16#FF): BOOL as TRUE or FALSE (also 1 or 0); integers as decimal numbers (42, -7); REAL and LREAL with a dot (3.5, 1e-3); TIME, LTIME and TOD as [d.]hh:mm:ss[.fffffff] (00:00:01.5 for 1.5 s); DATE as yyyy-MM-dd; DT as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss; enums as the member name (any case, the exact spelling wins) or its number; STRING and WSTRING as is, without quotes. Writes are governed by the user setting iecode.ads.aiWrites: off (default) refuses with a note how the user can enable it, confirm asks the user for each write, auto writes without an IECode prompt (but asks while the workspace settings change the ADS target or port). Every write is logged.

value.description: New value as plain text, e.g. TRUE, 42, 3.5, 00:00:01.5 (TIME) or an enum member name.
